prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1081; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured driver reporting a low-speed head-on collision with another vehicle earlier today. The claimant is now represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage start date.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene and matches the reported sequence of events. Responding officers and a witness statement are consistent with this.

Entry 4: Photos taken at the scene confirm several details of the collision. No independent witnesses have come forward beyond those already noted, so the photos and the report are the main sources for the event.

Entry 5: Vehicle damage was inspected and matches the described impact direction and speed. The file shows no earlier damage to this vehicle in prior claims or inspection records.

Entry 6: Claimant's reported neck strain is plausible for a collision of this type. Medical records show a small strain to the same area several years ago that fully healed, which is noted for context.

Entry 7: Claimant's account has remained the same in every conversation with the adjuster and counsel, including the initial statement and the follow-up call.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a usual course for this type of injury and tapered off as the claimant improved. Records show steady progress with no unexplained gaps in care.

Entry 9: Reviewed the file with the supervisor. The injury, treatment, and vehicle damage are consistent with the reported loss, and the claim will proceed to evaluation with counsel's demand package.
